keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. The page gives infobox 61,355 km2 (no year) and 60,391 km2 in the text, and no extent for any earlier date; a 140 km circle about Bikaner (about 61,500 km2, ratio 1.0) stands in for all years, so the early growth from the Jat country of Jangladesh (1465) to the 20th-century state is not drawn. The Rao Bika page says he left at his death in 1504 "a territory which comprised 40,000 square miles of land and about 3,000 villages" (about 103,600 km2, ratio 1.7 to the circle, inside the factor-of-two check, but the page names conquered places (Sirsa, Ladnu, Bhatner, Bhatinda, Singhana, Rini, Nohar, Pugal) without dates, so no earlier or larger shape is drawn).

wars.note: "On 30 September 1465, the 27-year-old Rao Bika, leading 100 horsemen and 500 foot-soldiers" left Jodhpur for Jangladesh (so the founding year 1465 is the departure year); the page says Jangladesh "was inhabited by Bhatis, Jats, Bhattis and Johiyas" and that Godara Jats supported Bika. Conquered places Sirsa, Ladnu, Bhatner, Bhatinda, Singhana, Rini, Nohar and Pugal are named without dates; the page is silent on Jaitsar and Deshnok.

notes: Four pages opened (Bikaner State first, then Rao Bika, Surat Singh of Bikaner and Ganga Singh). Bikaner State dates the founding (1465), the Mughal suzerainty of Rao Kalyan Mal (1542-1571), the British protectorate (9 March 1818) and the accession (7 August 1947) but no territorial gain or loss: not the 1542 Jodhpur occupation, the Bhatner/Hanumangarh conquest of 1805, or the entry into Rajasthan (1949). The mughal-empire and british-empire/british-raj dossiers should carry the vassal events for bikaner-state (Mughal vassal from the reign of Kalyan Mal, British protectorate from 9 March 1818 to 1947). The end year 1947 is the accession, not the merger into Greater Rajasthan (1949, not on the page). The shape is the late state throughout (floor and ceiling unknown). Three more pages opened: Rao Bika (departure 30 September 1465; 40,000 square miles at 1504, against 61,355 km2 on the state page; conquered places undated), Surat Singh of Bikaner (the 9 March 1818 treaty with Metcalfe, "subordinate co-operation"; silent on Bhatner and any conquest; the Hanumangarh Fort page returned url_not_found) and Ganga Singh (succeeded 16 December 1888 although the table says 1887; Sutlej canal built in his reign and Sikh settlers of the 1920s; silent on territory). Still needed from a later pass: the 1805 Bhatner/Hanumangarh conquest, the 1542 Jodhpur occupation (Rao Maldeo), and the 1949 merger into Rajasthan.
